snapshot.title: TNPSC Geography: Resources & Energy
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC GS Hook: Wind: Muppandal. Lignite: Neyveli. Pichavaram: Cuddalore. Kudankulam: Russia. Dharmapuri: Forest.

quick_notes.title: Mineral Wealth (Recap)
quick_notes.detail: Lignite (Neyveli - largest in India). Magnesite (Salem). Bauxite (Shevaroy hills).
quick_notes.explanation: India has many valuable minerals found in different regions. Lignite is a type of soft brown coal used for electricity, and the largest deposit in India is located at Neyveli in Tamil Nadu. Magnesite is a mineral used to make heat-resistant bricks and is mainly mined in Salem, Tamil Nadu. Bauxite is the main ore from which aluminum is made, and it is found in the Shevaroy Hills of Tamil Nadu. These three locations are important sources of these specific minerals.

quick_notes.title: Renewable Energy
quick_notes.detail: TN is a global leader. 1st in Wind Energy (Muppandal, Aralvaimozhi). Large Solar plants (Kamuthi, Ramanathapuram).
quick_notes.explanation: Tamil Nadu is a global leader in renewable energy, which means electricity generated from natural sources that never run out, like wind and sunlight. The state produces the most wind energy in India, with large wind farms at Muppandal and Aralvaimozhi where tall turbines spin to make power. Tamil Nadu also has huge solar power plants in Kamuthi and Ramanathapuram that use sunlight to create electricity.

quick_notes.title: Thermal & Nuclear
quick_notes.detail: Nuclear: Kudankulam (Tirunelveli - Indo-Russian), Kalpakkam (MAPS). Thermal : Ennore, Mettur, Thoothukudi.
quick_notes.explanation: Thermal and Nuclear Power Plants in Tamil Nadu Nuclear power plants use the energy released from splitting atoms to generate electricity. The Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant is located in Tirunelveli district and is a joint project between India and Russia, meaning it is an Indo-Russian collaboration. The Kalpakkam Nuclear Power Plant, also known as Madras Atomic Power Station or MAPS, is located near Chennai and is India's own facility. Thermal power plants burn fuels like coal to produce electricity. The major thermal power plants in Tamil Nadu are located at Ennore near Chennai, at Mettur in the Salem district, and at Thoothukudi in the Thoothukudi district.

quick_notes.title: Forest Resources
quick_notes.detail: Total Forest Cover ~20.21%. Largest forest area : Dharmapuri. Mangroves : Pichavaram (Cuddalore - 2nd largest in world).
quick_notes.explanation: Forest cover means the percentage of land in a state or country that is covered by trees and forests. In Tamil Nadu, the total forest cover is about 20.21% of the state's total land area. The district with the largest area of forest is Dharmapuri, which has more forest land than any other district in Tamil Nadu. Mangroves are a special type of trees and plants that grow along coastlines in salty water, and the Pichavaram mangrove forest is located in Cuddalore district. Pichavaram is the second largest mangrove forest in the entire world. So, when you study forest resources in Tamil Nadu, remember that about one-fifth of the state is forested, Dharmapuri has the biggest forest area, and Pichavaram mangroves are a globally important coastal forest.

quick_notes.title: Wildlife
quick_notes.detail: Mudumalai (Nilgiris), Anaimalai (Top Slip), Guindy (Chennai), Gulf of Mannar (Marine).
quick_notes.explanation: Wildlife means the animals and plants that live in nature. A wildlife sanctuary is a protected area where animals can live safely without being harmed by humans. Mudumalai Wildlife Sanctuary is in the Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu, known for elephants and tigers. Anaimalai Tiger Reserve, also called Top Slip, is a protected forest in the Coimbatore district. Guindy National Park is a small park located inside Chennai city, home to deer and snakes. Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park is a protected area in the sea along the Tamil Nadu coast, where coral reefs and sea animals like turtles and dolphins are safeguarded.
